title: Quell batch amplification and tenant starvation caused by interleaved long-context requests
creator: Leah Martinez
description: Multiple customers reported sustained p99 token latency regressions and intermittent request timeouts when tenant mixes include frequent short requests interleaved with a small proportion of very long-context sessions. The root cause is an amplification interaction between the continuous batcher admission policy and KV-cache eviction behaviour in multi-tenant hosts. Symptoms seen across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket tracks investigation, fix design, PRs, canary and rollout coordination, and post-deployment validation.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create mixed workload: 80% short requests (<=64 tokens), 20% long requests (>=8k context) across two tenant queues.
2) Configure continuous-batcher with adaptive admission reservoir enabled (default).
3) Run steady traffic with microbursts (2-5x baseline) from short-requests tenant while long-requests tenant continues producing slow generations.
4) Observe scheduler admission skew, queue starvation for short flows, increased p99 latency and KV cache thrash events in logs.
investigation_notes: - Reproduced locally and in a dedicated canary cluster using the customer's traffic replay from AcmeSearch (sanitized).

- Root cause: adaptive reservoir mis-estimates available admission capacity when a small number of long-context requests hold KV cache slots and extend GPU work, which leads to batch amplification: many small requests accumulate behind long ones causing head-of-line delays.
- Secondary cause: eviction hysteresis too aggressive; KV evictions triggered on transient memory pressure caused cascading cold-kv misses and extra prefetch loads, amplifying tail latency.
- Observed tick-edge scheduling drift where admission window renewals batch at tick boundaries, creating short intervals of starvation for latency-sensitive tenants.
- Affects Hosted (multi-tenant pools) most severely, Dedicated when mixed workloads share GPUs, and Private when autoscaler-cordon events coincide with mixed-length batches.
- Logged signals: admission_denied_count, kv_eviction_rate, batch_wait_ms, tenant_starvation_alerts.
decisions: 1) Implement short-request priority lane in the admission controller rather than special-casing by size only — keeps small interactive flows low-latency without completely starving long flows.
2) Add dampening factor to adaptive reservoir (exponential decay over 200ms window) to avoid rapid oscillation from microbursts.
3) Introduce temporary KV pinning heuristic: stable hot keys for active short flows are pinned for 2s to prevent eviction churn during transient bursts.
4) Fix tick-edge drift by staggering admission renewals across 10ms jitter per worker tick.
5) Incremental rollout: canary -> throttled cross-region -> full region.
proposed_fix: Combine three coordinated changes: (A) admission controller: add a priority lane for latency-sensitive short requests + reservoir dampening with decay window; (B) KV cache: implement short-flow pinning and increase eviction hysteresis for recently accessed small-request keys; (C) scheduler: add jitter to admission renewals and a fast-path preemptive dequeue for pending short batches when long batches exceed configured GPU-hold threshold.
canary_plan: Canary on 3 hosts in us-west-2 hosted pool with mixed synthetic traffic mirroring customer mixes for 48 hours. Enable detailed telemetry and a high-sensitivity alert for any increase in p99 over baseline. Start with admission-priority-lane only for first 12 hours, then enable KV pinning and jitter in second 12-hour window.
canary_results: 12h stage 1: p95 improved 8%, p99 improved 28% for short-request tenants; admission_denied_count for short flows dropped by 90%. Stage 2 (after enabling KV pinning + jitter): sustained p99 improvement 42%, kv_eviction_rate down 65%, no increase in GPU utilization beyond 3% overhead. No customer timeouts observed in canary hosts. Observability dashboards: runtime-1.22/canary-145678.
rollout_plan: 1) Tag runtime-1.22-canary and deploy to 5% of production hosts in non-critical region.
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback if short-flow p99 regresses by >10% for more than 5 minutes or if KV eviction rate increases beyond baseline by >30% for 15 minutes. Rollback steps documented in runbook link.
customer_notes: Affected customers identified and notified: AcmeSearch (support-3821), Boxly (support-3972), FinLedger (support-4010).
Provided mitigations: tenant-level admission caps, temporary routing to isolated Dedicated pools for FinLedger and Boxly while fix is validated.
Follow-up scheduled with AcmeSearch on 2026-03-16 for validation and acceptance testing.
